title: Prerequisite
content:
Before starting the deployment and lab implementation, the following prerequisites must be prepared:
AWS Account: A valid AWS account is required to access and manage cloud services such as EC2, RDS, and S3. Region: The system is deployed in ap-southeast-2 (Sydney) to ensure compatibility and stable performance. Tools: - AWS Management Console (main interface for resource configuration) - SSH client (Git Bash / Terminal) to connect to EC2 instance - SCP (Secure Copy Protocol) to transfer source code from local machine to server - Composer to install AWS SDK for PHP (used for S3 integration) IAM Permissions: The following permissions are required: - Amazon EC2 Full Access - Amazon RDS Full Access - Amazon S3 Full Access - IAM permission to create Access Keys These prerequisites ensure that the deployment process can be performed efficiently and securely.

title: Project Format and Tools
content:
Recommended Format The project is implemented in the form of a technical workshop-style documentation, following a structured and step-by-step approach. The content is organized similarly to a deployment guide, enabling readers to reproduce the system on AWS. The report structure is inspired by the FCAJ workshop template on GitHub, including clear sections such as Overview, Architecture, Implementation Steps, Testing, and Clean-up. The project is presented in a bilingual format (English and Vietnamese) to ensure accessibility and clarity. Tools & Requirements The project meets the required criteria as follows:
Bilingual Content: All main sections are presented in both English and Vietnamese to ensure clarity and completeness. Structured Documentation: The report follows a clear structure including Proposal, Worklog, Workshop, and Evaluation sections. Architecture Visualization: System architecture diagrams are created to illustrate the interaction between AWS services (EC2, RDS, S3). Code Snippets: Relevant code segments such as database connection (PHP), IAM policies, and configuration steps are included. Supporting Files: Deployment-related configurations (e.g., SQL scripts, setup commands) are provided where applicable. AWS Services Used: The project utilizes multiple AWS services, including EC2, RDS, and S3, satisfying the requirement of using at least three services.

title: Worklog
content:
This page presents the work log for the Classic Groove project, broken down by week and day.
The work log helps track progress, completed tasks, and any issues that need to be addressed during the development of the declaration system.
The project will be completed within 8 weeks (2 months), with the goal of building and developing a complete web application on a cloud-based operating system (AWS).
Week 1: Studied AWS fundamentals and core services (EC2, RDS). Created AWS account and configured IAM user with least privilege.
Week 2: Analyzed project requirements and prepared local development environment using LAMP stack. Built and tested MySQL database locally. Week 3: Provisioned EC2 instance (Amazon Linux 2), configured Security Group (SSH, HTTP, HTTPS), and created SSH key pair. Installed Apache and PHP. Week 4: Uploaded project source code using SCP and deployed to Apache web root (/var/www/html). Configured file permissions and tested application via public IP. Week 5: Created Amazon RDS (MySQL) instance, configured Security Group for database access, and enabled public access. Connected EC2 to RDS and imported database using SQL dump.
Week 6: Troubleshot database connection issues, including MySQL 8 compatibility and charset errors. Installed php-mysqlnd and upgraded PHP version. Created test script (testdb.php) to validate EC2–RDS connection.
Week 7: Configured database connection in application source (dataProvider.php) using mysqli_real_connect with SSL. Restarted Apache and validated full system functionality. Week 8: Performed system testing and debugging. Verified all application features and database operations. Documented deployment process and prepared final report.

title: Architecture & Design
content:
Architecture Design: The system follows a 3-tier architecture model including presentation layer (EC2), data layer (RDS), and storage layer (S3). The architecture diagram clearly illustrates data flow between components.
Service Selection:
EC2: Flexible compute service for hosting PHP application RDS (MySQL): Managed database for reliability and scalability S3: Scalable object storage for static assets Reason for Selection: Services are selected based on ease of deployment, managed capabilities, cost efficiency, and suitability for traditional web applications.
Security & IAM:
Security Groups used to restrict access (SSH, HTTP, MySQL) IAM principles applied (least privilege) No hard-coded credentials in source code Scalability & Operation:
Architecture supports scaling by upgrading EC2 instance or using load balancing (future work) Basic monitoring via logs and system testing

title: Proposal
content:
Classic Groove Web Application Deployment on AWS 1. Overview The project focuses on deploying the “Classic Groove” web application – an online platform for browsing and purchasing classic music records – onto the AWS cloud infrastructure. The system is built using PHP and MySQL, and will be hosted on Amazon EC2, with Amazon RDS handling database services and Amazon S3 storing static resources such as images and media files.
2. Goals Deploy a fully functional web application on AWS. Ensure high availability, scalability, and security. Optimize performance for both dynamic and static content delivery. Gain hands-on experience with core AWS services (EC2, RDS, S3). 3. Problem to be solved The application is initially developed in a local environment, which lacks scalability, accessibility, and reliability. Key challenges include deploying the system to a cloud environment, configuring secure database connections, and improving performance when handling user requests and static resources.
4. Architecture Solution The system architecture consists of:
Amazon EC2: Hosts the PHP web application. Amazon RDS (MySQL): Manages relational database. Amazon S3: Stores static files (images, assets). Data flow: Client → EC2 (Web Server) → RDS (Database) & S3 (Static Content)
5. 8 Weeks Timeline Week 1–2: AWS fundamentals & local environment setup (LAMP, requirement analysis) Week 3–4: EC2 provisioning, configuration & web application deployment Week 5–6: RDS setup, database migration & optimization Week 7: S3 integration for static asset storage Week 8: Testing, security hardening & project documentation 6. Budget estimate The project utilizes AWS Free Tier services where applicable:
EC2 (t2.micro / t3.micro) RDS (db.t3.micro) S3 (low-cost storage) Estimated cost beyond Free Tier: approximately $5–10/month depending on usage.
7. Risk assessment Security misconfiguration (Security Groups, IAM policies) Unexpected AWS costs due to improper resource usage Network latency between EC2 and RDS Data loss without proper backup strategy

title: Step-by-step
content:
The deployment process includes the following steps: Step 1: Create EC2 (Web Server) Step 2: SSH & Install Apache + PHP Step 3: Upload Code to EC2 Step 4: Copy to Web Root Step 5: Connect Database (RDS) Step 6: S3 (Image Upload)
Create EC2 (Web Server) Objective Create a virtual server on Amazon Web Services to:
Host and run the PHP web application Serve as a deployment environment for the project Detailed Steps
Access EC2 Service Log in to AWS Management Console Search for EC2 Click Launch Instance Set Instance Name Name: classic-groove-server Choose Operating System (Important) Select: Amazon Linux 2 Choose Instance Type Instance type: t3.micro; Eligible for Free Tier (no cost) Create Key Pair (for SSH access) Click: Create new key pair Configuration: Name: aws-key Type: .pem Download the key file and store it securely (important for SSH access) Configure Network Settings Enable: Allow HTTP traffic (port 80) Allow HTTPS traffic (port 443) SSH: Keep default setting (My IP) AWS will automatically create a Security Group Configure Storage Keep default: 8 GB Launch Instance Click: Launch Instance SSH + Install Apache + PHP Connect to EC2 via SSH Open terminal (or Git Bash) Step 1: Navigate to the directory containing the .pem (Example (Windows Git Bash): cd Downloads )
Step2: Set permission for the key file chmod 400 aws-key.pem
Step 3: Connect to the EC2 instance ssh -i aws-key.pem ec2-user@<public-ip>
Example: ssh -i aws-key.pem ec2-user@13.211.2555.184
Update the system sudo dnf update -y
Install Apache and PHP sudo dnf install httpd php php-mysqlnd -y
Start and enable Apache service sudo systemctl start httpd sudo systemctl enable httpd
Verify web server Open browser: http://public-ip Expected result: The Apache Test Page is displayed, indicating that the web server is running successfully. Example: http://13.211.255.184
Upload code to EC2 The easiest way to upload source code is by using SCP (Secure Copy Protocol).
Step 1: Open terminal on your local machine (not inside the EC2 instance).
Step 2: Execute the following command to upload the project: scp -i aws-key.pem -r Classic-Groove ec2-user@13.211.255.184:/home/ec2-user/
Explanation: + Classic-Groove: the project folder on the local machine + /home/ec2-user/: destination directory on the EC2 server
Expected result: The project source code is successfully transferred from the local machine to the EC2 instance.
Copy to web root Return to the EC2 instance via SSH and deploy the application to the web root directory.
Step 1: Run the following command to copy source code to the Apache web directory: sudo cp -r ~/Classic-Groove-main/* /var/www/html/ Step 2: Set appropriate permissions: sudo chmod -R 777 /var/www/html Step 3: Verify the deployment. + Open a web browser and access: http://13.211.255.184 Expected result: The web application is successfully deployed and accessible via the public IP address.

Upload image to S3 Receive URL Store in database Display image directly from S3 Conclusion: User upload → S3 stores file → PHP retrieves URL → DB stores URL → Web loads image from URL
Successful upload URL: https://classic-groove-images.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/xxx.jpg
Summary S3: The system successfully integrates Amazon S3 for image storage. Uploaded images are stored as objects in S3 and accessed via public URLs. This approach eliminates local server storage, improves scalability, and enhances performance for handling static assets in the system.

title: Workshop
content:
Triển khai ứng dụng “Classic Groove” trên nền tảng AWS Workshop overview This workshop demonstrates how to deploy the Classic Groove PHP web application on AWS using a three-tier architecture. The system leverages Amazon EC2 for application hosting, Amazon RDS (MySQL) for database management, and Amazon S3 for static asset storage. The solution ensures scalability, reliability, and basic security for a production-like environment.
Prerequisite AWS Account Basic Linux & Apache knowledge SSH client (Terminal / PuTTY) MySQL client PHP web source code Architecture Description Architecture components:
EC2: Hosts PHP web application RDS (MySQL): Managed database service S3: Stores static assets (images, media) Flow: Client → EC2 → RDS → S3 Security:
Security Group restricts access (HTTP, SSH, MySQL) IAM Role (optional) for EC2 to access S3 Implementation Steps Step 1: EC2 Setup
Launch EC2 (Amazon Linux 2) Configure Security Group (22, 80, 443) Install Apache, PHP Step 2: Deploy Web Application
Upload source code via SCP Move to /var/www/html Restart Apache Step 3:
Create MySQL RDS instance Enable public access Open port 3306 Import database Step 4: Connect EC2 to RDS
Update DB config in PHP Test connection (test script) Step 5: S3 Integration
Create S3 bucket Upload images/media Update application to load assets from S3 Step 6: IAM Policy (Optional but recommended) Example policy for EC2 to access S3:
{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["s3:GetObject"], "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::your-bucket-name/*" } ] } Step 7: Testing & Validation
Access website via public IP Verify database CRUD Check static assets load from S3 Step 8: Clean-up
Terminate EC2 Delete RDS instance Remove S3 bucket Delete unused resources Content Format & Tools Requirements Architecture & Design Implementation Testing & Monitoring Optimization & Clean-up

title: Self-Assessment
content:
During my internship at Công ty TNHH Amazon Web Services Viet Nam from 09/03/2026 to 02/05/2026, I had the opportunity to learn, practice, and apply the knowledge I gained at school to a real-world work environment. I participated in projects using AWS services such as EC2, VPC, RDS, S3, and IAM. Through implementing a 3-tier system, I gained a clear understanding of how to build a complete web system on a cloud platform.
Specifically, I learned how to:
Provision and configure EC2 instances for web hosting (Apache, PHP) Set up and manage databases using Amazon RDS (MySQL) Configure networking with VPC and Security Groups for secure communication Integrate Amazon S3 for static asset storage Apply IAM policies following the principle of least privilege Additionally, I improved my debugging and troubleshooting skills by resolving real-world issues such as database connection errors, charset problems, and environment misconfigurations.
In terms of soft skills, I developed self-learning ability, problem-solving skills, and time management while ensuring project completion within the given timeline.
In terms of work ethic, I always strived to complete tasks well, complied with workplace regulations, and actively engaged with colleagues to improve work efficiency.
To objectively reflect on my internship period, I would like to evaluate myself based on the following criteria:
No. Criteria Description Good Fair Average 1 Professional knowledge & skills Understanding of the field, applying knowledge in practice, proficiency with tools, work quality ☐ ✅ ☐ 2 Ability to learn Ability to absorb new knowledge and learn quickly ☐ ✅ ☐ 3 Proactiveness Taking initiative, seeking out tasks without waiting for instructions ✅ ☐ ☐ 4 Sense of responsibility Completing tasks on time and ensuring quality ✅ ☐ ☐ 5 Discipline Adhering to schedules, rules, and work processes ✅ ☐ ☐ 6 Progressive mindset Willingness to receive feedback and improve oneself ☐ ✅ ☐ 7 Communication Presenting ideas and reporting work clearly ☐ ✅ ☐ 8 Teamwork Working effectively with colleagues and participating in teams ✅ ☐ ☐ 9 Professional conduct Respecting colleagues, partners, and the work environment ✅ ☐ ☐ 10 Problem-solving skills Identifying problems, proposing solutions, and showing creativity ☐ ✅ ☐ 11 Contribution to project/team Work effectiveness, innovative ideas, recognition from the team ✅ ☐ ☐ 12 Overall General evaluation of the entire internship period ✅ ☐ ☐ Limitations Despite the achievements, the internship also revealed several limitations and challenges.
The first challenge was adapting to a cloud environment. Transitioning from local development to AWS required understanding how different services interact, especially EC2, RDS, and VPC. Misconfigurations in Security Groups or connection settings often caused system failures. The second challenge involved troubleshooting technical issues such as MySQL connection errors, charset mismatches, and missing PHP drivers (mysqlnd). Resolving these issues required extensive research and experimentation. The third limitation was system design thinking. Initially, I focused on functionality rather than considering scalability, cost optimization, and security. Additionally, my ability to quickly understand advanced cloud concepts and technical documentation in English still needs improvement. Overall, these limitations mainly stem from adapting to a new environment and technology stack, but they also provided valuable learning opportunities.

title: Sharing and Feedback
content:
Overall Evaluation 1. Working Environment
The Working environment is quite comfortable and friendly. People are easy to communicate with and willing to help when I encounter difficulties, even outside of working hours. The workspace is also tidy and conducive to concentration.
2. Support from Mentor / Team Admin
The mentors were very dedicated, explaining things clearly when I didn’t understand and always encouraging me to ask further questions, which helped me gain a deeper understanding. The admin team also provided quick support with documentation and related issues.
3. Relevance of Work to Academic Major
The AWS internship and project provided invaluable practical experience. I gained a better understanding of how to deploy web applications on the cloud through services such as EC2, VPC, RDS, S3, and IAM.
4. Learning & Skill Development Opportunities
During the process, I encountered quite a few problems that required me to figure out how to solve them myself. This helped me improve my debugging skills and technical thinking. At the same time, I realized that I need to learn a lot more if I want to pursue this field long-term.
5. Company Culture & Team Spirit
Everyone works in a relaxed yet serious manner when needed. When there’s an urgent task, everyone supports each other to get it done. This makes me feel comfortable and not overly stressed.
6. Internship Policies / Benefits
The company provides internship allowances and flexible working hours when needed. Additionally, participation in events helps gain valuable practical knowledge.
Suggestions & Expectations For the University: I suggest that the Faculty incorporate more practical cloud computing courses and hands-on labs related to AWS services into the curriculum. Organizing more industry-sponsored workshops or seminars would also help students bridge the gap between academic theory and real-world industrial demands.
For the Company / Internship Program: The internship program was highly valuable. I recommend that the company continue to expand the scope of mentorship to include more deep-dive sessions on “Infrastructure as Code” (IaC) tools like Terraform or CloudFormation. Furthermore, providing more opportunities for interns to participate in the entire lifecycle of a production project would significantly enhance our practical problem-solving skills.
